market_summary: The completed US equity session is constructive but selective, based on 1747 articles from Yahoo Finance, Stocktwits, MarketBeat, Kalkine Media, simplywall.st. The dominant theme is macro, with 799 macro items, 481 company items, 410 industry items, and 57 policy items. The tape looks more useful for identifying near-term rotation and risk appetite than for making a single directional index call.
macro_summary: Late Cycle Markets are balancing easier policy expectations against growth and earnings risk, keeping leadership narrow and confirmation dependent. The market is taking its direction from Fed/rates, with investors testing whether policy support can offset slower growth and earnings risk. Macro coverage is concentrated around Fed/rates (228), inflation (129), oil/energy (100), growth/jobs (56). The practical implication is that equity rallies may need confirmation from rates and inflation expectations; if yields rise while growth headlines weaken, risk appetite can fade quickly.
risk_summary: Sentiment is constructive but selective: 295 positive, 235 negative, and 1217 neutral articles. My read is to avoid treating headline volume as conviction by itself; the more important signal is whether macro-sensitive and technology-sensitive stories are pointing in the same direction.
